title: A country is entitled to decide how many people it admits each year
oneLiner: A claim about sovereignty, not about any particular number.
body: Whatever the economic arguments, proponents hold that the size of the intake is a legitimate democratic decision, and that it is reasonable for the government to set a figure and manage the programs to meet it.
contextBackground: Almost everyone in the debate accepts this in principle, which is why it does little to settle the question of what the number should be. It is here because it is often stated as if it did.
contextDisagreement: The principle is barely contested. The disagreement is whether invoking it adds anything to an argument about a specific cap, which is a question about this connection rather than about the claim.

otherClaim.title: Net overseas migration should be held below 200,000 a year

claimItself.title: Net overseas migration should be held below 200,000 a year
claimItself.oneLiner: Whether the federal government should cap net arrivals below the levels of the past decade and well below the post-pandemic peak.
claimItself.body: Net overseas migration is arrivals minus departures of people who stay, or leave, for at least twelve months. It averaged just over 200,000 a year in the decade before the pandemic and exceeded 500,000 in 2022–23. The proposal is a cap of 200,000, which would require the government to manage the student, temporary-work and permanent programs together to hit it.
